summary: Add guarded custom-category deletion and complete reordering using AnyList's proven update-v2 multipart wire contract.
reason: Live disposable-fixture probes proved that category-group operation class 4 persists on POST /data/shopping-lists/update-v2 when the operations protobuf is sent as an application/octet-stream multipart part. Deletion uses the full category record as the removal set; reordering uses identifier-only category records in the requested complete order. The CLI now exposes both operations with preview-first apply gates and fresh read-back verification.

live_evidence.transport: multipart/form-data; operations part with application/octet-stream PBListOperationList

delete.payload: updatedCategoryGroup copied from the stored group; categories contains the full PBListCategory record(s) to remove
delete.result: persisted and verified by fresh stable-ID absence read-back

reorder.payload: updatedCategoryGroup copied from the stored group; categories contains identifier-only PBListCategory records in the complete desired order
reorder.result: persisted and verified by fresh stable-ID order read-back

live_evidence.cleanup: All disposable probe lists and categories were removed and independently verified absent; no production data was changed.

gate_state: Custom category deletion and reordering are live-supported. Category-group create, rename, and delete remain unsupported.
verification: go test -p 1 ./... (known sandbox socket-permission failures remain in unrelated httptest tests)
CLI preview and JSON smoke checks for categories delete and categories reorder
invariants_held: Every live mutation requires explicit --apply and fresh read-back verification.
System categories are rejected by both the CLI and lower-level client before any request.
The old non-persistent v1 route and remove-category handler are never used.
Reorder rejects duplicate, missing, unknown, empty, or incomplete orders.
No secrets, tokens, personal identifiers, or production fixture names are recorded.
